precepts.text: Whom shall I send, and who will go for us? Here am I; send me. That is the mindset of a leader, the same as David asking where Goliath was while everyone else cried about the situation.
precepts.point: The first mark of a leader's mindset: he believes he can get the job done. When an issue arises you do not run; you raise your hand, volunteer, and find the solution.

note.label: Mindset Of A Leader, Actions Of A King

precepts.why:
Job 33:23 speaks of “a messenger with him, an interpreter, one among a thousand”. You are the interpreter, brother, and you are that one among a thousand. When you are one among a thousand, that makes you a leader, and you have to have the mind of a leader. Any place you step into, your mindset shouldn't be to fit in; you should be figuring out how to make it better. Joseph didn't go into Egypt and just sit there; he asked how we are going to solve the problem. The Lord gave us wisdom, discretion, judgment and skill sets.

The first thing in the mindset of a leader is that he believes he can get the job done. That is what separates you from everybody else. When an issue arises, you don't run. You raise your hand, you volunteer, you figure out a solution to the problem.

Isaiah shows it: “Also I heard the voice of the Lord, saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” Who is going to go on our behalf? “Then said I, Here am I; send me.” That's the mindset of a leader.

That is the same thing David did. Everybody kept crying about the situation, and David said, where is Goliath at? Show me. The first thing you have to have is a willingness and a belief in completing the task, whatever it may be, and that mindset alone sets you apart. That is what the Lord has put in your spirit to do: not an unsure mind that says maybe I can, but send me.

precepts.text: Make the heart of this people fat and shut their eyes, lest they see and convert and be healed.
precepts.point: Leaders of other camps do not show up at IUIC schools unannounced and then complain on video about not being let in. There are channels; call first. The camps do not fellowship because of doctrine, and one GMS member sat in a school for months living a double life.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
The mist of darkness is reserved for those who speak evil of dignities and hate their brothers. Isaiah shows where that darkness comes from: “Go, and tell this people, Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not. Make the heart of this people fat, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes”. Shut their eyes: darkness.

Why? “lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and convert, and be healed.” Convert means repent. Lest they repent. The Lord shuts the eyes of the builders, the rulers, so they cannot see.

That is why Peter calls them “wells without water”, with no understanding. When you badmouth Peter, Paul, John the Baptist or any of the apostles and prophets, the Lord puts the spirit of darkness on you until you become a borderline, if not full-blown, Christianity teacher. Your ears are made heavy and your eyes are shut, and you cannot understand even the basic verses. Be mindful how you deal with brothers; brothers who murmur and speak evil bug out and go back into the world.

precepts.text: Hear ye indeed but understand not; the Lord makes their heart fat and shuts their eyes lest they see and convert.
precepts.point: The hearing ear and the seeing eye, the Lord has made both. When you battle with someone who does not understand, it is not their time; the Lord dulls the ears and closes the spiritual eyes so they cannot see or understand.

note.label: Proverbs 20: Integrity, Just Weights, and Waiting on the Lord

precepts.why:
“The hearing ear, and the seeing eye, the Lord hath made even both of them.” Hearing and seeing come from the Lord, and so does the lack of them.

Isaiah was sent with that very message: “Go, and tell this people, Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not.” The Lord makes their heart fat and shuts their eyes, lest they see and convert. They have ears and eyes, but no understanding comes through them, because the Lord has closed them.

So when you battle with someone who does not understand, it is not their time. The Lord dulls the ears and closes the spiritual eyes so they cannot see or understand. He made the hearing ear and the seeing eye, and he decides when they open.

precepts.text: Christ spoke in parables so that seeing they see not and hearing they hear not, fulfilling the prophecy of Isaiah.
precepts.point: Christ spoke in parables because it is not meant for everybody to get the understanding of the bible. Captain OC's class, The Purpose of Christ Told by the Israelites, opens this in detail.

note.label: Isaiah 6: The Prophet's Vision and Commission

precepts.why:
“Make the heart of this people fat, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes; lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and convert, and be healed.” Christ carried this out with parables: “Therefore speak I to them in parables: because they seeing see not; and hearing they hear not, neither do they understand. And in them is fulfilled the prophecy of Esaias, which saith, By hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing ye shall see, and shall not perceive”.

Christ spoke in parables so that seeing they see not and hearing they hear not, and in them the prophecy of Isaiah is fulfilled. It is not meant for everybody to get the understanding of the bible. Captain OC’s class, The Purpose of Christ Told by the Israelites, opens this in detail.

precepts.text: Hear ye indeed but understand not; their eyes are shut lest they convert and be healed.
precepts.point: The eyes of them that see shall not be dim and the ears of them that hear shall hearken; you will begin to see spiritually and hear with understanding. The heart of the rash shall understand knowledge and the stammering tongue shall speak plainly.

note.label: Isaiah 32: A King Shall Reign in Righteousness

precepts.why:
“And the eyes of them that see shall not be dim, and the ears of them that hear shall hearken.” That is the undoing of what Isaiah was sent to say at the first: “Go, and tell this people, Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not. Make the heart of this people fat, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes; lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and convert, and be healed.”

Their eyes were shut and their ears made heavy lest they convert and be healed. Isaiah 32 is when that is lifted: you will begin to see spiritually and hear with understanding. “The heart also of the rash shall understand knowledge, and the tongue of the stammerers shall be ready to speak plainly.”

precepts.text: Hear ye indeed, but understand not; make the heart of this people fat, lest they convert and be healed.
precepts.point: They saw the works and did not perceive. The heart was made fat and the ears heavy so that they would not be converted, because judgment had to come.

note.label: Matthew 13: The Parables of the Kingdom

precepts.why:
“And in them is fulfilled the prophecy of Esaias, which saith, By hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing ye shall see, and shall not perceive”. Here is that prophecy as it was given to Isaiah: “Go, and tell this people, Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not. Make the heart of this people fat, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes; lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and convert, and be healed.”

They saw the works and did not perceive. Isaiah was told to make the heart of this people fat, make their ears heavy and shut their eyes, lest they convert and be healed. It was done to them on purpose, so that they would not be converted, because judgment had to come. Matthew says the same: their heart is waxed gross, their ears are dull of hearing, their eyes they have closed, “lest at any time they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and should understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them.” That is why he spoke to them in parables, and why the ones who heard him and saw his works did not understand.
